conventions.convention: Semiconvexity with coefficient λ means that subtracting λ|u|²/2 gives a convex function; supporting inequalities therefore contain +λ|v−u|²/2.
The potential-subdifferential growth bound controls its minimum element norm, equivalently the existence of a bounded supporting selection. It does not bound the domain normal cone.
R need not be convex. Its differential is uniformly Lipschitz on bounded sets and bounded on each R-sublevel set.

L² label spaces are Hilbert for arbitrary probability label spaces, but separability is asserted only under countable generation. Euclidean label dimension and vector output dimension are independent.
The flow velocity is the negative minimum of the full shifted constrained subdifferential, rather than the smooth gradient plus a separately minimized potential subgradient.

Strong Wasserstein subgradients use every coupling with a uniform small-action remainder. Generalized-geodesic inequalities retain the specified plan cost, which need not equal the squared endpoint W2 distance.
AC is explicit in the Hilbert, characteristic, transport and flow results. AC² locally on [0,∞) includes square-integrable action on each [0,T].

The general existence and particle-limit results require initial laws in a common cutoff Q_r0. They give compact-time deterministic W2 stability, without a stochastic sampling rate or an SGD conclusion.
Particle subgradients are Euclidean Fréchet subgradients; the weighted inner product is m⁻¹Σ x_i·y_i, so the particle inclusion is x′ ∈ −m∂F_m.

load_bearing.statement: The feature energy is F(μ)=R(∫Φ dμ)+∫V dμ when the measure is concentrated on Ω and both integrals exist finitely, and +∞ otherwise. Its hypotheses include a separable real Hilbert feature space, differentiable R and Φ, semiconvex nonnegative V, and the stated nested convex cutoff, regularity and bounded-selection growth conditions.

Under AC and the feature-energy hypotheses, the localized lift is proper, lower semicontinuous and lower bounded on any probability label space. Its Hilbert subdifferential is precisely the smooth feature gradient plus square-integrable pointwise constrained potential subgradients. The full shifted minimum S(a,u) is jointly Borel, bounded by A_r‖a‖+M_r, and gives the minimum-norm Hilbert subgradient.

Assume AC. A proper, lower semicontinuous, bounded-below λ-convex energy on a separable real Hilbert space generates, from every finite-energy initial point, a unique locally AC² subgradient flow. It satisfies the energy identity, selects the minimum-norm subgradient almost everywhere, and contracts distances by e^(−λt).

Assume AC and the feature-energy hypotheses. Continuous prescribed forcing yields unique forward constrained characteristics, jointly continuous in time and starting point and locally Lipschitz in the starting point. Finite-action PDE solutions are their pushforwards. Two self-consistent solutions concentrated on D∩Q_r satisfy W2(μ_t,ν_t)≤e^((C_r−λ_V)t)W2(μ_0,ν_0).

Under AC and the feature-energy hypotheses, the smooth localized lift has the displayed first-order gradient and gradient Lipschitz constant L_r A_r²+N_r B_r on C_r, for arbitrary probability labels. The full lift is consequently (λ_V−L_r A_r²−N_r B_r)-semiconvex.

Assume AC. If a continuous path x:[0,T]→H in a separable real Hilbert space has finite supremum C(x) of its partition quadratic energies, then x(t)=x(0)+∫₀ᵗu(s)ds for a strongly measurable L² derivative u, x is norm-differentiable almost everywhere, and ∫₀ᵀ‖u‖²=C(x).

Under AC and the feature-energy hypotheses, every finite-energy initial probability concentrated on Q_r has a unique localized AC² flow with the prescribed constrained minimum velocity. It satisfies the energy identity, the EVI with λ_r=λ_V−L_r A_r²−N_r B_r, and W2 contraction by e^(−λ_r t).

Under AC and the feature-energy hypotheses, for initial laws concentrated on Q_r0 the stated radius r(T) bounds the localized flow on [0,T] whenever the cutoff R exceeds r(T). The added cutoff constraint is then inactive relative to Ω, and all such localized flows agree on [0,T].

Under AC and the full feature-energy hypotheses, a finite-energy initial probability concentrated on Q_r0 generates a unique global AC² locally Wasserstein flow with the prescribed Ω-constrained minimum velocity. It has finite-horizon cutoff bounds and the energy identity. Two starts in the same cutoff with a common initial-energy bound satisfy the stated compact-time W2 stability estimate.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplied coupling, optimal-plan, finite-action continuity-equation, superposition, AC² and minimum-velocity interfaces against their actual uses. AC, narrow continuity, Borel velocities, finite action and finite second moments are retained. The distance-derivative argument uses superposition and disintegration with the stated conditioning direction.

Checked downstream citations to the feature-energy definition, prescribed-forcing characteristics, finite-horizon confinement, global flow and particle convergence. The separation consumers supply their common-cutoff/model hypotheses and use forward continuous characteristics. The particle/time-limit theorem retains the separate mean-field energy-convergence assumption and does not infer global optimization from finite-time W2 convergence.
